La deuxième moitié de l’année 2023 a été: The second half of 2023 was particularly difficult for some Jewish communities in Montréal and across Canada.
Le 9 novembre, la métropole montréalaise: On November 9, the city of Montréal woke up to a surprise: the streets were blanketed with the year's first snowfall. But residents of the Côte-des-Neiges and Outremont neighbourhoods woke up to news that was colder than the weather: the doors of two Jewish elementary schools had been riddled with bullets.
Quelques jours plus tôt, c’était une syn: A few days earlier, a synagogue in Dollard-des-Ormeaux, in the West Island, had been targeted in a Molotov cocktail attack.
Rapidement, des politiciens et des perso: Politicians and public figures quickly condemned these antisemitic acts. Throughout Montréal's Jewish community, these horrors rang in families' ears like a gunshot. Adding to the voices condemning the acts were those of organizations such as the Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA), which also pointed out that it <l1>seeks to represent the diversity of Jewish perspectives across Canada.</l1>
À la suite des événements survenus le 7: Following the events of October 7, 2023, in the Middle East, tensions have emerged, involving institutions, public figures and civil society alike. Heated exchanges have been filmed, notably during demonstrations and gatherings at universities, and have circulated on social media.
Aujourd’hui, au centre de toutes ces ten: Today, at the centre of all these tensions, accusations of antisemitism are being heard. Yet even the definition of the word struggles to be recognized and accepted unanimously.
Pour beaucoup, la signification du terme: For many people, the meaning of the term “antisemitism” remains unclear. In 2016, the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) produced its own working definition of antisemitism:
‍<strong>« L’antisémitisme est une certa: ‍“Antisemitism is a certain perception of Jews, which may be expressed as hatred toward Jews. Rhetorical and physical manifestations of antisemitism are directed toward Jewish or non-Jewish individuals and/or their property, toward Jewish community institutions and religious facilities.”‍
À quoi s’ajoute ce qui suit :: To which the following is added:
<strong>L’antisémitisme peut se manifest: Antisemitism may include the targeting of the State of Israel when it is perceived as a Jewish collectivity. However, criticism of Israel similar to that levelled against any other state cannot be regarded as antisemitic. Antisemitism often involves accusing Jews of conspiring against humanity and, in so doing, holding them responsible for “all the world's problems.” It is expressed in speech, in writing, in visual forms or through actions, and draws on sinister stereotypes and negative character traits.‍
L’adoption de cette définition au Canada: The adoption of this definition in Canada has been controversial. While motions to adopt it have been proposed in cities across the country, it has faced criticism for being too restrictive and for wording that could limit criticism of the Hebrew state.
<l1>En 2020, la Ville de Montréal a reje: <l1>In 2020, the City of Montréal rejected a motion calling for recognition of this definition.</l1> The move somewhat surprised those who had campaigned for the motion, since the Quebec and Canadian governments had already adopted the definition in their anti-racism strategies.
La mairesse Plante avait alors justifié: Mayor Plante had justified the City's decision by citing the discontent of Independent Jewish Voices Canada and the Fondation canado-palestinienne du Québec, which feared an infringement on freedom of expression, since the definition limited criticism of the State of Israel as a political entity.
Alors que la guerre sévit à Gaza, nombre: With war raging in Gaza, many people have recently been publicly accused of antisemitism. <l1>Students, professors, politicians and organizations that have criticized Israel's policies or accused the Hebrew state of violating human rights have been accused of antisemitism.</l1>
La crainte que la définition de l’IHRA p: There is concern that the IHRA definition could silence potential criticism of the actions of the State of Israel in a context of war crimes and human rights violations.

Lisa Grushcow is based at the Temple Emanu-El-Beth-Sholom, in the borough of Westmount, in Montréal. She welcomes us on a Friday around noon, a few hours before sunset marks the start of Shabbat, the weekly day of rest in the Jewish tradition.
Ce qui, en ces temps d’incertitude, fait: What makes Lisa Grushcow such an important figure for her community in these uncertain times is that she represents a way of being Jewish that differs from tradition. “I am the rabbi of a Reform synagogue that has existed since the 19<sup>th</sup> century,” she points out at the very start of our meeting. In her office, a Pride flag can be seen next to the flag of Israel. In addition to being a woman, the rabbi is a lesbian and divorced.
Consciente de l’importance de son rôle à: Aware of the importance of her role at a moment in history like the one we are living through, the rabbi calls on her community to embrace humanity and collectivity rather than division and withdrawal. “I feel like antisemitism has always been present,” she begins. With a cup of freshly hand-brewed coffee in front of her, she explains that she takes the time to respond gently and calmly to the comments directed at her throughout the media in connection with her role as a rabbi. “I've never felt unsafe here in Montréal. Today, I have to think about my safety and the safety of my community at a time when it's important for us to come together. It shouldn't be like this,” she confides.
Au sujet des crimes haineux qui ont eu l: On the hate crimes that took place in Montréal last fall, the former McGill University student prefers to appeal to altruism rather than distrust: we must “build bridges, not walls.” She notes, however, that she is aware of the explosive nature of the war in the Middle East and the turmoil it can create, even thousands of kilometres from the conflict.
« Être passionné, c’est bien. Mais cela: “Being passionate is good. But that doesn't excuse everything, and it doesn't allow everything. The end never justifies the means,” she says in a firm tone.
La rabbin insiste toutefois sur une dist: The rabbi insists, however, on an important distinction. For her, criticizing the Israeli government is in no way a form of antisemitism.
« Je suis loin d’être fan du gouvernemen: “I am far from a fan of the Netanyahu government,” she continues. She adds that before October 7, she actively supported the protests in Israel against his government. “Today, I demonstrate for Israel and for the safety of the Jewish community.”
Toute la différence réside dans l’intent: The whole difference lies in the intention behind the criticism, she believes. “When we criticize, we criticize out of love. We know that [Israel] can be a better homeland. I think it becomes difficult when people criticize out of hatred.”
Dans le même ordre d’idées, elle questio: Along the same lines, she asks: “Why are all these people going to such lengths to criticize Israel? Often these are the very same people who don't say a word about human rights conditions elsewhere in the world. That's when I consider it a form of antisemitism,” she explains.
Elle déclare aussi que des slogans comme: She also says that slogans such as “From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free,” which can be heard at gatherings or demonstrations in Montréal and elsewhere in the world, can be hurtful. “It means there is no place for Jews in Israel… It implies that we have no legitimacy there,” she laments.

Lorsqu’on lui pose la question, Lisa Gru: When asked, Lisa Grushcow answers that the Jewish community “is not so divided on the question of Israel's existence: there are many different opinions about the Israeli government and Israeli policy, yes, but there is a consensus on the legitimacy of Zionism as the right of the Jewish people to have a homeland in the State of Israel.”
‍<l1>Cet avis n’est toutefois pas partag: ‍<l1>This view is not shared by everyone in Montréal's Jewish community, however.</l1>
Yakov Rabkin, professeur émérite de l’Un: Yakov Rabkin, professor emeritus at the Université de Montréal and author of books on Zionism and Jewish studies, is among those who disagree with this statement. For him, “Jews are surely more divided by the question of Israel than by any other question.”
L’idée d’associer la critique d’Israël à: The idea of equating criticism of Israel with a form of discrimination against Jews goes back several decades, the expert explains. “This idea comes from Abba Eban, a former Israeli diplomat and foreign minister in the 1970s. He launched a campaign, backed by Israeli propaganda bodies, aimed at associating criticism of the country with antisemitism, at a time when, in the aftermath of the Second World War, antisemitism had become unacceptable,” he says. “Over time, this idea caught on. And to make that happen, Jews had to be associated with Israel.”
Autrefois connu comme « la Voix d’Israël: Once known as “the Voice of Israel,” Abba Eban served as Israel's foreign minister from 1966 to 1974. He alone embodied “hasbara,” a word that refers to both Israeli diplomacy and propaganda. He is often described as a “public relations machine” for the government and for Israel's image internationally.
C’est dans cette optique, rappelle le pr: It is in this spirit, Professor Rabkin points out, that “associating all people of Jewish faith with the State of Israel has allowed Israeli policies to enjoy a certain immunity from criticism.”

Après avoir entendu de nombreux politici: After hearing many Western politicians address members of the Jewish community using expressions like “your state, your country” (referring to Israel), Mr. Rabkin understands why, for many people, criticism of Israel has “become, by the same token, anti-Jewish criticism.”
D’ailleurs, l’auteur affirme que « cette: The author also says that “this association of the Jewish community with Israel has made Jews hostages of Israel's actions.” “Those who don't distinguish between ‘Jewish’ and ‘Israel’ are only grist for Zionism's mill.”
Il exprime donc son désarroi face à la c: He therefore expresses his dismay at the condemnation by the <l1>Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA)</l1> of the antisemitic acts committed in Montréal. “I find it outrageous that CIJA supports Israel and, at the same time, is outraged that Jews are being attacked, when they themselves have placed Israeli flags in every Jewish institution,” he exclaims. “I completely understand that Jews identify with Israel—like any political opinion, it's legitimate. Pour lui, l’antisémitisme est qu’une for: For him, antisemitism is just one form of racism and xenophobia like any other. “We don't need a special definition of antisemitism. What matters is not to see antisemitism as a separate kind of racism, but as one version of racism,” he concludes.

Mélissa Shriqui est membre de la synagog: Mélissa Shriqui has been a member of the Temple Emanu-El-Beth-Sholom synagogue since birth. She is also an active member of Montréal's Jewish community. She confides in La Converse about her concerns regarding antisemitism and its connotations in the current context of heightened tensions.
La citoyenne partage sa peur et son ango: The Montrealer shares her fear and anguish over the antisemitic acts that occurred in early November. “I'm going through worrying times, times that scare me, but also that hurt me. These acts have no place in Montréal, they have no place in Quebec,” she says firmly.
« Depuis le 7 octobre, on voit que l’har: “Since October 7, we can see that harmony is rather hard to find. The Jewish community has really been wounded.” She also feels that, in her daily life, there is now a “before and after October 7.”
Aujourd’hui, la définition de l’antisémi: Today, the IHRA definition of antisemitism keeps gaining popularity. Over the past few months, dozens of organizations around the world have adopted it. As we noted earlier, the City of Montréal suspended the adoption process, wishing to “find its own definition of antisemitism, adapted to the metropolis,” as the mayor said at the time.
Dans un ultime effort de conscientisatio: In one last effort to raise awareness, Rabbi Grushcow comes back to us and weighs her words to convey the full importance of humanity and humility. Although she has spent years coordinating with religious leaders across Quebec, she reiterates the need to build ties between communities in order to limit hate speech.
« Nous avons tous nos limites, mais parf: “We all have our limits, but sometimes we set them too quickly,” the rabbi says in closing. She acknowledges that she is aware of her own limits, but still believes it is possible to coexist in a world where her community has the right to self-determination.
En se dirigeant vers la sortie du temple: As she heads toward the exit of the temple, guarded by a bodyguard, she takes a moment to go back in and reflect in the empty synagogue, where photos of the Israeli hostages held by Hamas have been placed on the pews.
